question: A 37-year-old man is brought to the emergency department after being attacked with a knife. Physical examination shows a 4-cm laceration in the midline of the right forearm. An MRI of the right arm shows damage to a nerve that runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles. Loss of sensation over which of the following areas is most likely in this patient?

options.opa: Palmar surface of the little finger

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Injury to nerve between superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles -> Damage to the median nerve -> Loss of sensation in the palmar surface of the little finger -> opa: Palmar surface of the little finger -> 95%

CHAIN: Injury to nerve between superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles -> Damage to the median nerve -> Loss of sensation in the palmar surface of the thumb, index, and middle fingers -> opa: Palmar surface of the little finger -> 90%
analysis: Based on the description of the injury and the nerve affected, the most likely area to experience loss of sensation would be the palmar surface of the little finger, as this corresponds to the distribution of the ulnar nerve which runs between the superficial and deep flexor digitorum muscles.
